implementation.name: Idris 2
implementation.version_scope: Idris 2 tutorial using the Chez Scheme backend.

fit.text: Type-driven programs and proofs; this profile covers Idris 2 rather than Idris 1.

prerequisites.text: Learn typed functions and modules; the tutorial explains the IO type.

execution.text: The default compiler generates an executable using the Chez Scheme backend.

behavior.text: The REPL checks types and evaluates expressions before an executable is built.

tooling.text: The REPL, --check and package options support iterative development.

maintenance.text: Keep the selected backend and package dependencies aligned with the compiler.

costs.text: The compiler license permits redistribution under its stated conditions; backend dependencies need separate review.

example.code:
module Main

main : IO ()
main = putStrLn "PLLDN"
example.run_instructions: With Idris 2 and its Chez backend installed, run idris2 hello.idr -o hello, then run build/exec/hello.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

implementation.name: OpenJDK
implementation.version_scope: Conventional Java class and javac/java workflow; JDK distribution and version must be selected independently.

sources.label: JDK language, runtime and deployment learning paths

fit.text: Java applications using JVM APIs; JavaFX desktop applications and runtime images have dedicated learning paths.

prerequisites.text: Install a JDK and learn classes, methods and the main entry point; an IDE is optional for the first program.

execution.text: Compile Hello.java with javac, then execute the class with java Hello in a compatible runtime.

behavior.text: The language learning path covers types, objects, exceptions and modules; the JVM has its own garbage collection and security tools.

tooling.text: Use JDK build and diagnostic tools; JFR and jlink support observing applications and creating runtime images.

maintenance.text: Select a concrete JDK distribution and check its update policy; a generic Java label does not identify the runtime being shipped.

costs.text: OpenJDK source licensing and a vendor's subscription/support offering are different scopes; the learning site links these separately.

example.run_instructions: With a JDK installed, run javac Hello.java followed by java Hello.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: The exception applies only to files carrying the applicable notice; the JDK distribution includes other component notices.
licenses.notice: Inspect the chosen distribution and per-file applicability; this is not a blanket license for Java applications.

implementation.name: JavaScript on Node.js
implementation.version_scope: Server/command-line path; browser host APIs are a different deployment context.

sources.label: MDN JavaScript language and host environments

fit.text: Browser interaction and server programs; browser DOM APIs and Node.js server APIs belong to their respective hosts.

prerequisites.text: Start with variables, functions and objects; web work additionally needs the browser document model.

execution.text: Node.js runs JavaScript outside a browser. This example uses its command-line environment.

behavior.text: Types are dynamic and inheritance is prototype-based; Node.js offers asynchronous I/O in its runtime.

tooling.text: Node.js documentation covers npm, debugging, profiling and its built-in test runner.

maintenance.text: Choose a Node.js version and its supported ECMAScript features; browser support must be evaluated separately.

costs.text: Node.js is open source; budget server operation and any externally selected services separately.

example.run_instructions: With Node.js installed, run node hello.js. In a browser, the same statement writes to developer-console output.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: Core runtime grant; included third-party components retain their own notices.
licenses.notice: Read the complete distribution license file; JavaScript itself does not assign a license to your application.
